events.invalidation: RBA delivers or IB fully prices the remaining 50-60bp of tightening while housing/labor stop deteriorating.

INFERENCE: that residual hike path is a policy error into a housing bust and will be cut as labor/housing data stay weak; receiving the 2027 H1 AONIA strip is the cleanest slowdown expression. UNKNOWN: whether trimmed-mean 3.6%, the energy shock, or one more RBA hike lands before the housing channel dominates. Sidecar open_positions is empty, so this is a new OPEN versus the $100m cap, not an add to an existing IB position.

events.invalidation: IB 2027-03/06 holds or rises through 4.86-4.94 while housing and labor stop deteriorating and inflation stays hot enough to deliver the extra hikes.
events.rationale: FACT: AONIA cash is 4.35 as of 18-Sep-2026. Tradable IB contracts price Oct-26 4.565 (+21.5bp), Mar-27 4.86 (+51bp), Jun-27 4.94 (+59bp) and Jul/Aug-27 4.945 (+59.5bp). The owned AONIA_2027-06 paper mark is the 2027-03/06 strip average 4.9075. NSW stamp-duty receipts fell 24% y/y in August with transactions -18% and Sydney/Melbourne values more than 7% below peak. AU labor: unemployment 4.5% from 4.4%, employment -15.8k, WPI +3.2% y/y vs +3.4%. Activity: Q2 GDP +0.4% q/q, August business conditions/confidence softer. Consumer: Westpac-MI sentiment fell 5.2% to 84.4 on 16 Sep after a still-strong July spending print. Inflation score is 82, but July headline CPI eased to 3.5% from 3.8% while trimmed mean stayed 3.6%. AU 2Y/5Y/10Y sit at 4.999/5.041/5.348, all ~99th 1y percentile after a +26 to +39bp one-month sell-off. Desk thesis: energy shock is constraining the global easing impulse after Fed 25bp to 3.75-4.00, BoJ to 1.25%, and BoE 6-3 hold. Sidecar open_positions already holds long AONIA_2027-06 pos-3b40ade3da2c. INFERENCE: the market is still pricing almost two extra RBA hikes into 2027 H1 after the housing/labor/sentiment channel is already open; that is a policy-error slowdown discrepancy, and receiving the locked strip owns it more cleanly than short AUD. UNKNOWN: CFTC/CME positioning (packet status partial/null), post-cutoff RBA communication, executable IB depth on the thin H1-27 contracts, and whether global term-rate pressure plus inflation 82 forces the residual 50-60bp to be delivered anyway.
